cards.en: We prefer this table because we have a stroller.
cards.ja: ベビーカーがあるので、このテーブルがいいです。
cards.glossEn: We prefer this table because we have a stroller.

cards.en: What time does the reservation arrive?
cards.ja: 予約のお客さんは何時に来ますか。
cards.glossEn: What time does the reservation arrive?

cards.ja: 10時15分より前に食べ終えるのはいかがでしょうか。

cards.en: If possible, we would like to stay here.
cards.ja: 可能でしたら、この席に座っていたいのですが。
cards.glossEn: If possible, we would like to stay here.

cards.ja: わかりました。事情は理解しました。

reader.en: It is Saturday morning and my family is having breakfast at a big table by the window.
reader.ja: 土曜日の朝、私の家族は窓際の大きなテーブルで朝食を食べています。
reader.glossEn: It is Saturday morning and my family is having breakfast at a big table by the window.

reader.en: The server comes over and says: Excuse me, we have a reservation and we need this table.
reader.ja: 女性の店員がやって来て、こう言います。「すみません、予約が入っていて、このテーブルが必要なんです。」
reader.glossEn: The server comes over and says: Excuse me, we have a reservation and we need this table.

reader.en: She offers us a smaller table in the corner, near the counter.
reader.ja: 店員はカウンター近くの隅にある、もっと小さなテーブルを勧めてくれます。
reader.glossEn: She offers us a smaller table in the corner, near the counter.

reader.en: I calmly explain to her: We prefer this table because we have a stroller and it does not fit in the corner.
reader.ja: 私は落ち着いて説明します。「ベビーカーがあるので、このテーブルがいいです。隅の席にはベビーカーが入りません。」
reader.glossEn: I calmly explain to her: We prefer this table because we have a stroller and it does not fit in the corner.

reader.en: Then I ask her: What time does the reservation arrive?
reader.ja: それから店員に尋ねます。「予約のお客さんは何時に来ますか。」
reader.glossEn: Then I ask her: What time does the reservation arrive?

reader.en: The server answers that the group arrives at 10:30.
reader.ja: 店員は、そのグループが10時30分に来ると答えます。
reader.glossEn: The server answers that the group arrives at 10:30.

reader.en: So I propose: What if we finish breakfast here before 10:15 and then move to the patio for coffee?
reader.ja: そこで私は提案します。「10時15分より前にここで朝食を食べ終えて、そのあとコーヒーを飲むためにテラス席に移るのはどうでしょうか。」
reader.glossEn: So I propose: What if we finish breakfast here before 10:15 and then move to the patio for coffee?

reader.en: She smiles and says: Perfect, there is shade on the patio and I will bring you an extra chair.
reader.ja: 店員は笑顔で言います。「いいですね。テラス席には日陰がありますし、椅子をもう一脚お持ちします。」
reader.glossEn: She smiles and says: Perfect, there is shade on the patio and I will bring you an extra chair.

reader.en: I tell her: Thank you very much for your help, this way we are all happy.
reader.ja: 私は店員に言います。「ご協力ありがとうございます。こうすればみんなが満足できます。」
reader.glossEn: I tell her: Thank you very much for your help, this way we are all happy.

issues.note: English source explicitly says the server is female. Japanese 女性の店員 makes that explicit where needed; 店員 alone later avoids awkward repetition. Qualified Japanese reviewer should decide whether the marked gender is natural in this teaching context.

Source rincón is an inside corner near the counter, not a street corner. 部屋の隅 in the card and 隅 in Reader preserve this. The archived draft instead adds an aisle inspection not present in current source.
English patio means outdoor café seating here. テラス席 is a contextual candidate, not a general equivalence for every patio. Source Spanish terraza and locale need dictionary review.

The card says “We prefer”; Japanese ベビーカーがあるので、このテーブルがいいです expresses the group preference without an overt plural subject. Reader includes that the stroller does not fit the corner; card does not add that separate fact.

The English question says the reservation arrives, then Reader clarifies a group arriving at 10:30. Japanese question names 予約のお客さん, avoiding the unnatural claim that a booking itself walks in. Reviewer to assess equivalence.
Card finishes before 10:15; Reader finishes breakfast here before 10:15 and moves to the patio for coffee. Japanese keeps the time and sequence. Source says strictly before 10:15, not at or by 10:15.
Shade, an extra chair, and mutual satisfaction are retained. Japanese last line uses みんなが満足できます for “we are all happy”; reviewer to assess the satisfaction/happiness nuance.
Mesera/mesero, reservación/reserva, rincón/esquina, carriola and ¿Qué le parece si...? notes are Spanish-specific and remain internal. None are Japanese teaching.

Archived draft has 12 cards and nine dialogue turns with different people and aisle-safety facts. Candidate has 15 source-order cards and nine source-aligned Reader turns. Old rows have no explicit IDs; string overlap is text-only and neither saved-item nor audio migration is authorized.
